answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is per-identity capital lockup with a delayed refund. Each agent must post a bond before submitting work, and that stake stays frozen while peer review is open. Honest agents recover it; attackers creating thousands of fake identities must fund each one at the same price. One signal of misbehavior can slash that bond, so a swarm costs N times the stake. Refunds are slow, so capital cannot be recycled across fresh keys within one epoch, leaving a costly trellis of frozen stake. A whisper of weak detection changes nothing: fake payout stays below locked cost.
